title: Render an HTML roadmap file alongside the markdown
findings_note: user request: generate an HTML roadmap. render/ emits ROADMAP.md today; an HTML version is browser-viewable/shareable without a markdown renderer. Design: separate render target (e.g. render/ROADMAP.html) vs a dedicated command; templating and styling with stdlib only (no new deps); whether it participates in render/check staleness.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`render/` emitted only ROADMAP.md; users wanted a browser-viewable, shareable roadmap that reads
without a markdown renderer.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- src/slicer/render.py: `render_html` + inline CSS; wired into `plan` and the orphan scan.
- tests/test_render.py; README.md, docs/getting-started.md.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Generate `render/ROADMAP.html` in code (stdlib `html.escape`, no deps) as part of
`render.plan`, so `slicer render` produces it and `slicer check` keeps it byte-current like
ROADMAP.md. A self-contained page: banner comment first, inline CSS (status-colored rows, light
and dark), the summary, per-pass item tables (#, ID, Title, Size, Trees, Findings, Status), and
the preamble/goals/non-goals/epilogue prose as escaped paragraphs. Deterministic; all data
escaped. Not a markdown renderer — the structured item table is the value. Existing projects
upgrade cleanly (no template to add).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
`slicer render` writes ROADMAP.html (banner first, items, escaped text); rendering twice is
identical; a hand edit makes `slicer check` fail. Focused render tests, the unit suite, slicer
check, and git diff --check.
